verdict.rationale: WezTerm's documented `wezterm cli` subcommand talks to a running GUI or mux instance to spawn programs and manipulate tabs and panes. A recorded runtime probe confirmed a full headless agent loop: spawn returned a pane-id, send-text ran a command, get-text read the output back, and list enumerated panes. A community user independently confirms get-text dumps scrollback. Missing for 10: the pack has no in-depth first-party docs for individual subcommands (send-text/get-text arguments, output formats); first-party evidence is limited to the CLI overview line.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can let a coding agent programmatically drive the terminal itself — create panes, run commands, read output — through a documented control protocol or API

citations.quote: The _cli_ subcommand interacts with a running wezterm GUI or multiplexer instance, and can be used to spawn programs and manipulate tabs and panes.

`wezterm cli spawn --new-window` returned a pane-id, `wezterm cli send-text --pane-id N "echo PA_PROBE_OK"` delivered, `wezterm cli get-text` read the pane content back, `wezterm cli list` enumerated windows/tabs/panes; no GUI session required.
